01 The decisions that matter
- Separate 406 broad-audience broadcasts from 515 narrow-cohort broadcasts. Broad clicks average 1.97%;
narrow clicks average 16.32%. Their audiences and purposes differ sharply.
- Practical movement lessons are repeatable click candidates. B182, B294, B243 and B242 each generated 261-296
recorded clicks with concrete skill or movement promises.
- Recorded USD entries are concentrated: 83 of 921 broadcast rows have positive Revenue fields. This does not
establish the distribution of actual sales. B532's USD 4,000 is one source entry; overall Sales Analytics displays USD
676,005.
- High opens alone do not establish business success. Broad 2023 opens reached 45.08%, while its click rate was
0.71%; 2020 had 29.53% opens and 4.08% clicks.
- Do not declare a universal best day. On common years, the Wednesday-versus-Monday click gap shrinks to
0.014 percentage points after equalizing year composition.
- Customer access and promised resources attract clicks for functional reasons. KBL access C606 records 81/100
clicks; this is not a sales-subject benchmark.
- Treat reply-led stories as an instrumentation gap. Five explicitly reply-led, zero-captured-anchor broadcasts have
zero tracked clicks; reply and booking outcomes are absent.
- Keep Mike's personal, embodied coaching voice, but connect each message to one clearly measured next
action. The voice is a defensible editorial pattern; its causal sales effect is unproved.

08 Voice, subject lines and wording
All 922 broadcast versions were processed computationally. Full visible-text qualitative reading covered 67
purposely selected broadcast bodies: 65 broad and two narrow. This includes leaders, weak-click cases, reply-led
messages, recent topics and service-email counterexamples. It is a transparent evidence sample, not exhaustive
manual semantic labeling of every sentence. Sequence definitions and all 16 notification previews were also
reviewed.
The recurring editorial structure
- Start from a felt problem or lived experience: fatigue, stiffness, overwork, confidence, fatherhood or training
frustration.
- Translate the story into embodied coaching: energy, breath, movement quality, recovery, practice and
consistency.
- Use direct second-person language and a personal sign-off to make the message feel like coaching rather than
a detached bulletin.
- Borrow concrete authority from named practitioners, demonstrations, interviews or Mike's own learning
experience.
- Move toward a specific next step: watch a tutorial, use a resource, attend a workshop, explore a program, book a
conversation or reply.
These are observed writing characteristics. Their combination with successful examples makes them useful design
candidates; the archive does not isolate the incremental effect of voice from topic, offer, audience and timing.
Common language and the range of the demonstrated voice
Mike's practical-coach language repeatedly emphasizes movement quality, progressions, energy, longevity and
recovery. Conversational signals include "I hope you enjoy," "if you'd like," "let me know" and "with your success
in mind." Enthusiasm can be informal - "stoked," "rad," "super excited" and "Let's goooooo!" - while
men's-development messages draw on presence, integrity, ownership, brotherhood, purpose and discomfort. The
source does not establish that one writer authored every message, so this is demonstrated brand voice rather
than a verified private personality.

13 An evidence-based strategy
The operating principle
Preserve the personal coaching voice, then define the purpose and next action. Measure teaching by
resource consumption, conversation by replies/bookings and onboarding by activation. Financial rankings
require verified orders and an explicit reconciled attribution rule. Recorded clicks are engagement evidence,
not a substitute for that financial work.
What to repeat and improve
- Repeat as a test candidate: a concrete movement or felt-problem promise, a short explanation and one primary
resource destination. Evidence: B182, B294, B242 and S21 C821/C822.
- Keep personal story when it earns the bridge to an action. B99 connects experience to an explicit offer; B1167
connects vulnerability to a self-check resource. Story alone has weak year-adjusted association.
- Use specific offers and logistics: who it is for, what they get, price/guarantee where relevant, dates and the next
action. B1004 is a useful launch example.
- Treat urgency as a closing-stage test with negative-outcome guardrails. B86/B608 contain positive USD fields
and elevated unsubscribes; actual net commercial value and an urgency effect are unverified.
- Keep customer utility concise and direct. Access, expert bonus and workshop messages support a specific task;
do not inflate a sales benchmark with their click rates.
- Improve podcast packaging by foregrounding one reader problem, concrete benefit and a single primary
listening destination. The podcast group's historical metrics support testing packaging, not stopping the channel.
What to reduce or investigate
- Reduce the use of opens as the sole success target. Monitor action after the open and track replies/bookings
when those are requested.
- Investigate long generic offer stacks and repeated late-sequence pressure. S21 and S15 suggest weaker later
click engagement, but stage and topic are confounded.
- Avoid automatically filling the calendar with more sends. Current records do not establish the best contact-level
frequency.
- Do not reuse placeholders, inactive branches, countdown dates or event reminders without an operational
check. Saved templates are not approved live configuration.
- Avoid extrapolating sparse high-ticket revenue or tiny 1-10-person groups into a universal writing formula.
A practical voice specification
Write as an experienced coach speaking to one person: grounded, direct, reflective and specific. Open with a
recognizable situation or useful promise. Use lived experience when it adds credibility; translate it into a practical
lesson. Use familiar words, brief paragraphs and a clear action. Keep authority concrete through a named example
or demonstration. Avoid treating health/fitness marketing claims as independently verified facts.

14 Ninety-day test plan
Financial gate: do not use archived dollar-field rankings as actual sales rankings until order coverage,
refunds/rebills, currency and the campaign attribution rule are reconciled. Engagement tests can proceed as
separate proposals; they do not answer the unresolved total-email-revenue question.
Days 1-14 / Measurement and operational foundation
Define goal types and revenue attribution; add a way to count replies/bookings in future work; verify event dates,
link destinations, cohort exclusions and consent. Establish each message's job and a fixed observation window.
No source account changes are part of this report.
Days 15-30 / Concrete resource packaging
Compare a specific skill/problem promise against a broader benefit for the same resource. Keep audience, offer,
delivery window and body mostly constant. Primary: clicks per reported recipient. Guardrails: unsubscribes and
spam.
Days 31-45 / Podcast packaging
Compare episode-first packaging with problem-first packaging of a comparable episode. Preserve the actual
content and primary destination. Evaluate qualified listening action if available; otherwise clearly label tracked
clicks as a proxy.
Days 46-60 / Story-to-action bridge
Compare a concise personal story plus one explicit resource action with a direct teaching opening. Do not change
the offer and subject simultaneously. Track replies separately if the message asks for conversation.
Days 61-75 / Send-window block test
Compare two practical Pacific windows on comparable audience/offer blocks, rotating assignment. Historical
evening/midday associations are candidates, not proof. Avoid declaring a permanent winner from a single send.
Days 76-90 / Sequence expectation and later-step clarity
Test clear initial-series cadence wording and a shorter later resource/offer step. Keep existing customer
onboarding separate from prospect sales. Evaluate cohort progression and complaint counts in addition to clicks.
How to keep the experiment honest
Set a primary outcome before sending, define the cohort, and change one main element at a time. Where
feasible, randomize comparable people into mutually exclusive variants and keep offer/context fixed. Record
assignment and observation windows; do not stop early merely when a favorable result appears. Retain both
absolute counts and denominators.
Typical recent broad audiences are around 2,500 people. A split of about 1,250 per arm at a 2% click baseline
produces only about 25 clicks per arm. Detecting a small relative lift in one email is difficult. An approximate
independent two-proportion calculation for 2.0% versus 2.5%, two-sided 5% and 80% power, requires roughly
13,800 per arm - far larger than one typical send. Repeated comparable blocks can accumulate evidence, but
repeat recipients and offer changes require an appropriate analysis design.
The power example is a planning approximation, not a guarantee or a claim about the archive's statistical significance. With smaller
available samples, report counts, uncertainty and whether the practical difference justifies further testing.
